constraints: The netlist uses only simple Verilog gate primitives (and, or, xor, not, nand, nor) and continuous assign statements; no proprietary IP or encrypted cells.
The netlist and design brief are self-contained; no external files are required to understand or simulate the design.
Participants must not modify inputs/ files; all analysis output goes into submission/trojan_report.json only.
Optional cross-checking with yosys/iverilog/vvp is allowed but not required to produce the report.
expected_outputs: submission/trojan_report.json containing an infection verdict, a list of suspect node identifiers, and a rationale referencing the specific gate instances involved.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted trojan_report.json must be valid JSON containing at minimum the top-level fields: 'infected' (boolean), 'suspect_nodes' (array of strings, each string an exact gate instance name found in aes_sub_netlist.v), and 'rationale' (string).

Every string listed in 'suspect_nodes' must correspond to an actual instance name declared in aes_sub_netlist.v (i.e., it must be a substring match of a gate/wire instantiation identifier present in the file).
If 'infected' is true, 'suspect_nodes' must contain at least 2 entries; if 'infected' is false, 'suspect_nodes' must be an empty array.

The report must include a field 'primary_output_affected' (string) naming the primary output port of aes_sub_netlist.v (as declared in port_map.json) that the reported payload logic drives, or the empty string if 'infected' is false.

interface: Submission file: submission/trojan_report.json (UTF-8 JSON, single object, no wrapping array). Required top-level keys and types: 'infected' (boolean), 'suspect_nodes' (array of string instance-name identifiers exactly as they appear in inputs/aes_sub_netlist.v), 'rationale' (string, non-empty), 'primary_output_affected' (string, must equal one of the output port names listed in inputs/port_map.json, or '' if infected is false). Extra keys are permitted and ignored by the grader. inputs/aes_sub_netlist.v defines module aes_sub_datapath with ports matching inputs/port_map.json; participants read these inputs read-only and never modify them.
objective: You are given a gate-level Verilog netlist representing a small synthesized combinational/sequential module derived from an AES-like datapath, along with a design brief describing its intended function. Analyze the netlist structurally and functionally, then produce an analysis report classifying whether the netlist is infected with a hardware Trojan, and if so, list the specific suspect gate/node instance names that form the trigger logic and the payload logic. Your report must be a single JSON file placed at submission/trojan_report.json.
response_format: A single JSON object written to submission/trojan_report.json with exactly the keys described in 'interface' (additional optional keys allowed): infected: bool, suspect_nodes: [string], rationale: string, primary_output_affected: string.
